solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Young Conservative in Newcastle becomes business magnate

indicators.note: in places the young Conservative inside the city's nickname

parts.note: Toon is the local nickname for the city of Newcastle upon Tyne

explanation.surface: A Young Conservative from Newcastle grows up to become a big businessman.
explanation.walkthrough: TOON is Geordie dialect for 'town', and the nickname of Newcastle and its football club.
explanation.definitionFit: A tycoon is a wealthy, powerful industrialist, the very picture of a business magnate.

clue.text: Bird sitting on church, unknown and very small

indicators.note: in a down answer the bird sits on top of the following pieces

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
Y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: A tiny bird perches on a church roof, unidentified.
explanation.definitionFit: Titchy is British slang for tiny or minute.

clue.text: Punisher of naughty cheats — 'Sir'!

indicators.note: naughty suggests misbehaving letters jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A schoolteacher, addressed as Sir, disciplines pupils who cheat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'naughty' rearranges the letters of CHEATS SIR.
explanation.definitionFit: One who chastises punishes or scolds severely, so a chastiser is a punisher.

clue.text: Listed as one having a prolonged spell of good form

definitions.meaning: entered on a register or roll of names

definitions.text: having a prolonged spell of good form

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means enjoying a run of success, and literally it means entered on a register of names.

clue.text: It's good having a small old-fashioned lamp

parts.note: slight means small or slender, as in a slight figure

explanation.surface: Someone says it is nice to own a little antique lamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small' looks like S, but it gives the whole word SLIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Gas-fuelled lamps lit streets and homes before electricity, so they are now old-fashioned lighting.

clue.text: Giving the thumbs up to writer, I perform on stage maybe

parts.note: an author is a writer
singing is one example of performing on stage

explanation.surface: A writer gets approval to sing on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Authorising means giving official approval or permission, a thumbs up.

clue.text: Affair in Australia is ongoing

indicators.note: in means the answer lies within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Someone reports a love affair still going on in Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: A liaison is a secret sexual relationship, an affair.

clue.text: Smut produces scowl, putting Bill off

indicators.note: off, with putting, means the bill is taken away from the scowl

parts.note: a grimace is a twisted, scowling facial expression
AC is an abbreviation for account, a bill

explanation.surface: Seeing filth makes someone frown once the bill is dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting ... off' removes AC from GRIMACE. 'Smut' here means soot or dirt rather than obscenity.
explanation.definitionFit: Smut in its older sense is soot or dirt, which is grime.

clue.text: Country's imprisoning any number — jailers here are old-fashioned

indicators.note: imprisoning means the country locks the number inside

parts.note: Turkey is a country; with the 's it gives Turkey's
N is a mathematical symbol for any number

explanation.surface: A nation holding prisoners has outdated warders.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive 's supplies the S in TURKEYS.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnkey is an archaic word for a jailer, one who holds the keys.

clue.text: Put label round each bishop that may have got into hot water

definitions.text: that may have got into hot water

indicators.note: the label goes round, enclosing the other two pieces

parts.note: a tag is a label
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: An instruction to tie a label around a bishop who is in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Got into hot water' suggests trouble, but here it is literal: a teabag is dunked in hot water.
explanation.definitionFit: A teabag is something literally dropped into hot water to brew, punning on the idiom for trouble.

clue.text: Notice one held by guide as being less likely to fall over

indicators.note: held by means the notice and one sit inside the guide

parts.note: to steer is to guide
an ad, or advertisement, is a notice
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A sign gripped by a guide makes them more stable on their feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Steadier is the comparative of steady, describing something firmer and more stable.

clue.text: Something lacking in a cold salad? Tricky situation

definitions.text: Something lacking in a cold salad?
definitions.meaning: a potato salad is served cold, so a warm spud is what it lacks
an awkward issue nobody wants to handle

explanation.definitionFit: A hot potato is an idiom for a controversial, awkward matter, and literally a warm spud absent from potato salad.

clue.text: A group getting on, fellows over time being neglected

indicators.note: in a down answer the earlier pieces sit over the last one

parts.note: a band is a group, especially of musicians
on means moving along, getting on
men are fellows

explanation.surface: An ageing band of men is left forgotten over time.
explanation.definitionFit: Abandonment is the state of being deserted or neglected.

clue.text: A residue of lipstick maybe from second kiss?

parts.note: a peck is a quick kiss

explanation.surface: A trace of lipstick left behind after a second kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: A speck is a tiny spot or particle, such as a smudge of lipstick left on a cheek.

clue.text: Manly aviators flying for a charitable organisation

indicators.note: flying suggests letters scattered and rearranged in the air

explanation.surface: Macho pilots take to the air in aid of charity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' rearranges the letters of MANLY AVIATORS.
explanation.definitionFit: This Christian movement is famous for its charitable work with the homeless and poor.

clue.text: Bizarre 'tree dance' is performed again

indicators.note: bizarre suggests a strange, mixed-up arrangement of letters

explanation.surface: An odd dance around a tree is staged once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bizarre' rearranges the letters of TREE DANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Re-enacted means acted out or performed a second time.

clue.text: One controlling machine in drama, landing on hill

indicators.note: in a down answer the drama lands on top of the hill

parts.note: an opera is a sung drama
a tor is a rocky hill, especially on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A machinist appears in a play set on a hilltop.
explanation.definitionFit: An operator is someone who works or controls a machine.

clue.text: Like an unsophisticated saint — nothing more, nothing less

definitions.meaning: a saint is virtuous and an unsophisticated person is uncomplicated
an idiom meaning simply and only that

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means absolutely and only, while read literally it describes someone virtuous and uncomplicated.

clue.text: Princess about to meet worker? One senses something in the air

definitions.text: One senses something in the air

parts.note: an ant is a worker insect

indicators.note: about means the princess's name is turned round

parts.note: Anne is the Princess Royal, daughter of Elizabeth II

explanation.surface: A princess goes to meet a worker, sensing something in the air.
explanation.walkthrough: The Princess is the Princess Royal; the definition fits both an insect's feeler and a radio aerial.
explanation.definitionFit: An antenna is an aerial that detects radio signals, or an insect's feeler sensing its surroundings.

clue.text: Bone in food paste getting everyone upset

parts.note: pâté is a savoury paste of meat or fish

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means the word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: Someone finds a bone in their pâté and everybody is upset.
explanation.definitionFit: The patella is the kneecap, a bone at the front of the knee.

clue.text: Prince soon begemmed

parts.note: early can mean soon, before long

explanation.surface: A prince will shortly be adorned with jewels.
explanation.definitionFit: Pearly means adorned with pearls, gems from oysters, so begemmed.

clue.text: Cook rubbish

definitions.meaning: to cook meat in an oven
as a verb, to criticise severely

explanation.definitionFit: To roast is both to cook in an oven and, informally, to criticise or mock someone harshly.

clue.text: Book finally complete? Not quite

indicators.note: not quite means the phrase stops one letter short of complete

parts.note: at last means finally

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a book is finally finished, and finds it is not.
explanation.walkthrough: AT LAST loses its final T, 'complete? Not quite' saying it is one letter short.
explanation.definitionFit: An atlas is a book of maps.

clue.text: Rider and horse said to be in horrifying situation

indicators.note: said means the pieces are spoken, giving a word sounding the same

parts.note: a knight is a mounted rider and a mare is a female horse

explanation.surface: A mounted rider and their steed find themselves in a terrible fix.
explanation.walkthrough: KNIGHT (rider) plus MARE (horse), spoken, sound like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightmare is a terrifying dream, and by extension any awful, distressing experience.

clue.text: Story books requiring editor with special gift

parts.note: a tale is a story
NT is the New Testament, a collection of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A collection of stories needs an editor who has a real gift.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone talented has a natural aptitude or flair, a gift for something.

clue.text: Man on roof delivering abuse and beginning to riot

parts.note: to slate is to criticise harshly, to abuse verbally

indicators.note: beginning to means take only the first letter of riot

explanation.surface: A man up on the roof is hurling insults and starting a riot.
explanation.definitionFit: A slater is a tradesman who lays slates on roofs, so he works up on the roof.

clue.text: Resumes subjects for BA after vacation?

indicators.note: after places the degree subjects following the break

parts.note: a rest is a holiday or vacation
a BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree, so its subjects are arts

explanation.surface: A student takes up degree subjects again after the holidays.
explanation.definitionFit: To restart is to begin again, which is what resumes means as a verb.

clue.text: Showy marble protected from the elements?

parts.note: a taw is a large marble used for shooting in the game
something sheltered from rain stays dry

explanation.surface: A gleaming marble is kept indoors out of the weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Tawdry means cheap and gaudy, showy in a tasteless way.
